solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Burns may have consumed this witch, finally saving lives (6)

indicatorNotes.finally: what comes finally in a word is its last letter, so only the end of 'saving' is used

blocks.note: a hag is an ugly old witch

annotation.surface: A witch-hunt where the poet Burns might have eaten the witch to save everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: Burns is Robert Burns, the Scottish poet who wrote 'Address to a Haggis', not the burning of a witch; haggis is a Scottish dish of offal and oats cooked in a sheep's stomach.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by allusion: Burns wrote a famous poem to this dish, and it is eaten at Burns Night suppers in his honour.

entries.clue: Fuss over skin of buffalo in dish from the Philippines (5)

indicatorNotes.skin of: an animal's skin is its outside layer, so only the outer letters of buffalo are kept

blocks.note: ado = fuss, as in Much Ado About Nothing

annotation.surface: Someone complaining about the buffalo hide in their Filipino meal.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' simply puts the first piece above the second.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: this vinegar-and-garlic stew is often called the national dish of the Philippines.

entries.clue: Listening device set up to capture a tantrum in eatery (9)

indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, setting something up raises it so it reads from the bottom, turning it upside down
indicatorNotes.to capture: a captor surrounds its prisoner, so the outer word goes round the inner ones

blocks.note: a strop is British slang for a fit of temper

annotation.surface: A spy plants a bug in a restaurant to record someone's meltdown.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the listening device a spy's tool planted in the restaurant, but it is only a word to be turned over and opened up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain hypernym: this is a pub serving restaurant-quality food, one kind of eatery.

entries.clue: Rest during the day inside messiest apartment (6)

indicatorNotes.inside: the answer is found inside the next words, as a room is inside a flat

blocks.note: runs from the fourth letter of messiest across into the first of apartment

annotation.surface: Someone napping in the afternoon in a very untidy flat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inside' reads naturally as indoors, the place for the nap, which hides its role as the pointer to letters within the next words.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed Spanish word for the afternoon nap taken in hot countries, so a rest during the day.

entries.clue: Harsh criticism set back support group involving several families (8)

indicatorNotes.set back: something set back is moved backwards, so the word is written back to front

blocks.note: a tribe is a social group of related families

annotation.surface: A harsh review has damaged a family-support charity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set back' looks like the damage the criticism did, but it is the instruction to turn the support around.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bitter spoken or written attack is harsh criticism.

entries.clue: Go with guys and rent Downing Street shop (10,5)

indicatorNotes.Downing: downing a drink means swallowing it, so the word before takes in the word after

blocks.note: rent = tore, as in rent one's clothes

annotation.surface: Someone joining friends to rent a shop in Downing Street, home of the British Prime Minister.
annotation.walkthrough: Downing Street is not a place here: it splits into a verb meaning swallowing and an abbreviation to be swallowed.
annotation.definitionFit: A hypernym: this is a large shop divided into sections selling different goods.

entries.clue: Share out bananas in highbrow cinema (8)

indicatorNotes.bananas: bananas is slang for crazy, and crazy letters do not stay in order

annotation.surface: Handing out bananas at an art cinema.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the fruit being shared, but it is slang for crazy.
annotation.definitionFit: Used attributively for serious, often foreign or independent films, and for the cinemas showing them, so a highbrow cinema.

entries.clue: Provide counterargument to objection introduced by engineers (5)

indicatorNotes.introduced by: someone introduced by another comes after them, so the engineers go first

blocks.note: RE = Royal Engineers, a British army corps

annotation.surface: A debate in which engineers raise an objection.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a meeting of engineers; the definition is a phrase verb needing an object, matching the transitive answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to argue against a claim with evidence is to provide a counterargument to it.

entries.clue: Perhaps lead guitar heard on rock music (4,5)

indicatorNotes.heard: what is heard is the sound of the word, so a different spelling may fit

blocks.note: a bass guitar, said out loud
heavy metal is a kind of rock

annotation.surface: A band's lead guitarist playing over a heavy rock track.
annotation.walkthrough: Lead guitar is the surface; lead the element is the definition, and 'Perhaps' flags it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: lead, like iron or zinc, is a common metal as opposed to a precious one like gold.

entries.clue: Trap chaotic protest on pitch (7,3)

indicatorNotes.chaotic: chaos scrambles order, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the protest goes second

blocks.note: to lob is to pitch, throw high

annotation.surface: A disorderly demonstration on a football field.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' reads as a sports field but is a verb, to throw.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by hypernym: this wicker or mesh cage baited to catch shellfish is one kind of trap.

entries.clue: Head and Shoulders not working? (4)

blocks.note: a sculpture showing only the head and shoulders

annotation.surface: Asking whether a bottle of Head & Shoulders shampoo has failed.
annotation.walkthrough: Capitalised, Head and Shoulders looks like the dandruff shampoo brand; it is the part of the body a sculpted portrait shows.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a sculpture of the upper body, and the slang adjective for broken.

entries.clue: Bully office worker’s latest pen-pal? (8)

indicatorNotes.latest: the latest in a series is the one that came last, so the last letter of worker

blocks.note: an office is a religious service

annotation.surface: Someone bullying an office worker's newest pen-friend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Office worker' is one phrase in the surface but splits in two: office is a church service, and only the worker gives a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint, marked by the question mark: someone who shares the pen with you is literally a pen pal.

entries.clue: Tiny character entering square promptly (2,4)

indicatorNotes.entering: something entering goes inside, so the character is placed within the square

blocks.note: one is a square number, 1 x 1
Tiny Tim, the sick boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

annotation.surface: A small figure stepping onto a town square without delay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tiny character' reads as a small letter or symbol; it is a named character from fiction.
annotation.definitionFit: An adverbial phrase: arriving at the scheduled moment is doing something promptly.

entries.clue: Bottom’s strange head from Puck (4)

indicatorNotes.head from: the head of a word is its front, so the first letter

blocks.note: rum = odd, in old-fashioned British slang

annotation.surface: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, Puck gives the weaver Bottom a strange donkey's head.
annotation.walkthrough: Bottom is the Shakespeare character in the surface and the backside in the answer; the apostrophe-s is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the backside, usually of an animal, so a bottom.

entries.clue: You impose keeping record for one with alien beliefs (9)

indicatorNotes.keeping: what keeps something holds it, so the impose word holds the record

blocks.note: to foist something on someone is to impose it
a log is a record, like a ship's log

annotation.surface: Someone insisting you keep a record of a foreigner's beliefs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alien beliefs' suggests foreign or strange opinions; it means beliefs about beings from space.
annotation.definitionFit: A description with a pun: a student of UFOs often believes in visitors from space.

entries.clue: Sucker very shortly left with nothing (8)

indicatorNotes.shortly: said shortly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A gullible person soon walks away empty-handed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' reads as a dupe; it is a bloodsucker. Most as 'very' is as in 'most kind'.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the insect feeds by sucking blood.

entries.clue: Attempt pass on the wrong side? (9)

blocks.note: British driving slang for overtaking on the inside

annotation.surface: A driver trying to overtake on the wrong side.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain, overtaking is done on the outside lane; passing a car on its inside is the illegal-seeming opposite, named by analogy.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the formal verb for taking on a task, and the road term for passing on the inside.

entries.clue: Hammer home excessively large drop? (8)

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels
to shed is to drop, as leaves or hair

annotation.surface: Driving a point home, perhaps about an overly big fall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hammer home' looks like the phrase meaning emphasise; it is the place a hammer lives.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the garden hut where tools are kept is a hammer's home.

entries.clue: Perform universal blessing holding pound coin (8)

indicatorNotes.holding: to hold something is to contain it, so the blessing goes round the pound

blocks.note: U = universal, the British film rating

annotation.surface: Performing a blessing for everyone while holding a pound coin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pound coin' reads as one thing; pound is a single letter and coin is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by hypernym: this old Spanish gold piece, beloved of pirate stories, is a coin.

entries.clue: Ran around back of tropical valley (4)

indicatorNotes.around: turned around means facing the other way, so the word is written backwards
indicatorNotes.back of: the back of a word is its end, so the last letter

blocks.note: led = ran, as in ran a company, reversed

annotation.surface: Someone running round the back of a tropical valley.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ran around' looks like running in circles; it is a past tense meaning managed, turned around.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small wooded hollow is a little valley.

entries.clue: Arab second in line after enemy messed up (6)

indicatorNotes.second in: the second letter found in the word
indicatorNotes.after: one piece placed after another comes below it in a down clue
indicatorNotes.messed up: messed-up things are out of order, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An Arab soldier second in the line behind a disordered enemy.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram gives the country itself, and the extra letter turns it into the word for its people.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by hypernym: a person from this Arabian Peninsula country is an Arab.

entries.clue: Wine and beer mostly for entrance (6)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means not quite all, so the beer loses its last letter

blocks.note: port is a fortified Portuguese wine

annotation.surface: Drinks served at the door.
annotation.walkthrough: A plain two-drink charade; the only trick is clipping the beer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually for a grand doorway or gateway, so an entrance.

entries.clue: Part of pin starts to topple if bowling in alley (5)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the start of a word is its first letter, taken from each word that follows

blocks.note: first letters of topple, if, bowling, in, alley

annotation.surface: A skittle falling over in a bowling alley.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pin' is a bowling pin in the surface but British slang for a leg in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A part-for-whole definition: the shinbone is part of the leg, which old slang calls a pin.

entries.clue: Fresh parmesan for old warrior (8)

indicatorNotes.Fresh: something made fresh is made anew, so the letters are put together in a new way

annotation.surface: Freshly grated cheese served to a veteran soldier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' describes the cheese in the surface but asks for a new arrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a soldier armed with a spear belongs to the armies of the past.

entries.clue: Queen on social media platform is appropriate (5)

annotation.surface: A royal posting on social media, judged fitting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as the adjective, fitting; it is the verb, to take for oneself. In a down clue the queen sits on the platform.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: seizing territory for oneself is appropriating it.

entries.clue: Chimp initially leaving to scale branch (4)

indicatorNotes.initially: what comes initially comes at the start, so the first letter of chimp
indicatorNotes.leaving: a letter leaving a word goes out of it, so it is removed

blocks.note: to scale a wall is to climb it
the first letter of chimp is removed

annotation.surface: A chimpanzee setting off to climb up a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The chimp and the branch make a tidy jungle picture, hiding that the chimp contributes only a letter to throw away.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a large bough of a tree is a branch.

entries.clue: Party’s most amusing person ultimately the GOAT? (10)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so the end letter of 'the'

blocks.note: someone who is a real hoot is very funny
a nanny is a female goat

annotation.surface: The funniest guest at the party is the Greatest Of All Time.
annotation.walkthrough: GOAT in capitals looks like the slang acronym for Greatest Of All Time; here it is just the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: originally a folk-music gathering, now any lively party.

entries.clue: Go across empty supermarket, dizzy after finishing off cider (8)

indicatorNotes.empty: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters
indicatorNotes.after: dizzy comes after the cider letter in the answer
indicatorNotes.finishing off: the finish of a word is its end, so the last letter of cider

blocks.note: addle = muddled, confused, as in addle-headed

annotation.surface: Crossing an empty supermarket, giddy after finishing the cider.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's drinking tale supplies the order: the dizzy piece comes after the cider letter, not where it sits in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to sit or stand with a leg either side of something is to go across it.

entries.clue: Mountaineering kit in sack on rocks (3,3)

blocks.note: a drink on the rocks is served chilled over cubes
to sack someone is to fire them

annotation.surface: Climbing gear packed in a rucksack on a rocky mountain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On rocks' reads as climbing terrain; it is the barman's phrase for a chilled drink, and 'on' puts that piece first.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by hypernym: a climber's pick for cutting steps in frozen slopes is mountaineering kit.
